features.method: Walked 480 m along geometry:lhc-tunnel-ring (the merged OSM ring, accuracy_m 20) from the ATLAS interaction point -- taken as the middle node of LHC relation 9512017's insertion-1 segment (way 685422600), i.e. ring coordinate index 1 -- in the direction of increasing ring index (toward the Point 2/ALICE side, which OSM's own member order and insertion-2's 'ALICE' tag confirm is the '12' sector), per FASER's sourced siting '480 m downstream of the ATLAS IP in the unused service tunnel TI12' (src:colliders-lhc-faser-inspire-experiment-record). This anchors the derivation on the OSM ring (accuracy_m 20), not on the coarse campus-grade point recorded for LHC Point 1 (precision 500 m), so it does not violate the coarse-anchor rule. accuracy_m 60 m combines the ring's own accuracy with the straight-ring-arc-vs-actual-tunnel-path uncertainty; this is a single point, not a trace of the TI12 tunnel itself, since no source gives that tunnel's own path.
features.name: TI12 tunnel, FASER location (derived point)

provenance.locator: 480 m computed along geometry:lhc-tunnel-ring from ring index 1
provenance.note: Point only; not a tracing of the TI12 tunnel.
provenance.quote: FASER will be located 480 m downstream of the ATLAS IP in the unused service tunnel TI12

features.method: Walked 480 m along geometry:lhc-tunnel-ring from the same ATLAS interaction-point reference (ring index 1) in the direction of decreasing ring index (toward the Point 8/LHCb side, the '81' sector, confirmed by insertion-8's 'LHCb' tag), per SND@LHC's sourced siting '480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point, in the TI18 tunnel' (arXiv:2210.02784 abstract). unlocated.backlog: Locate the new HL-LHC shafts/caverns (e.g. PM18, PM15) via CERN's HL-LHC civil-engineering pages and add them as their own geometry records once sourced.
unlocated.reason: HL-LHC is an in-place upgrade of the existing LHC ring (drawn as geometry:lhc-tunnel-ring under accelerator:lhc), not a separate structure, so drawing a second ring would misrepresent it as a distinct tunnel. Its own new civil works (e.g. the new shafts and service caverns being added at Points 1 and 5) are not located by any source fetched this session.

unlocated.backlog: Search CERN's historical civil-engineering archive or a 1970s ISR design report for a site plan with a scale bar; georeference against the Meyrin buildings that still exist.
unlocated.reason: The Intersecting Storage Rings occupied part of the Meyrin site until 1984. No OpenStreetMap trace was found this session (three Overpass name searches for 'ISR'/'Intersecting Storage' in the Meyrin bbox returned zero elements), and no other fetched source gives coordinates or a civil-engineering plan for its tunnel.

unlocated.backlog: Find Linac2's building number/plan via a CERN historical-photo or civil-engineering page (it stood near the current Linac4/PSB area before demolition).
unlocated.reason: Linac2 (in operation 1978-2018, now decommissioned) has no OpenStreetMap building trace (a name search for 'Linac 2'/'LINAC2' in the Meyrin bbox returned zero elements this session) and no fetched CERN page gives its location or footprint.

unlocated.backlog: Ask CERN's GIS/survey group for the CAST platform's coordinates, or find an open-days site plan showing its position relative to Point 8.
unlocated.reason: CAST's telescope building near LHC Point 8/SR8. No OpenStreetMap trace was found this session (a name search for 'CAST' near Point 8, radius 1.5 km, returned zero elements) and the existing site record itself documents that no official page gives a coordinate more precise than the Point 8 campus point.

unlocated.backlog: Locate ECN3 via CERN's North Area civil-engineering/BE-DEP-EA public drawings, or a detector-paper survey coordinate from NA62 or NA48.
unlocated.reason: ECN3 is an underground cavern in the North Area fed by the P42/K12 beamlines (currently housing NA62). It is not a surface building, so it has no OpenStreetMap footprint of its own; only the outer Prévessin site fence (way 23722021, drawn as geometry:prevessin-site-boundary, context only) and 77 numbered surface buildings with no 'ECN3' name were found in this session's North Area extract. Drawing the whole Prévessin boundary as if it were ECN3's own shape would misrepresent a small cavern as occupying the entire campus.
